Subject: Welcome to NPTEL Online Course : Ethical Hacking
Content:
Dear Learner

Welcome to SWAYAM-NPTEL Online Courses and Certification!

Thank you for signing up for our online course "Ethical Hacking". We wish you an enjoyable and informative learning experience.

Details regarding the course:
Name of the course: Ethical Hacking 
Course url: https://onlinecourses.nptel.ac.in/noc26_cs157/preview
Course duration : 12 weeks 

The course will begin on 20 July 2026 When content is released on the portal, you will get an email alerting you.

CONTENT AND ASSIGNMENTS

Every week, about 2.5 to 4 hours of videos containing content by the Course instructor will be released along with an assignment based on this. Please watch the lectures, follow the course regularly and submit all assessments and assignments before the due date. Your regular participation is vital for learning and doing well in the course. This will be done week on week through the duration of the course.
Please do the assignments yourself and even if you take help, kindly try to learn from it. These assignment will help you prepare for the final exams. Plagiarism and violating the Honor code will be taken very seriously if detected during the submission of assignments.

ANNOUNCEMENT AND DISCUSSION GROUPS TO CLEAR DOUBTS:

The announcement group - will only have messages from course instructors and teaching assistants - regarding the lessons, assignments, exam registration, hall tickets etc.
The discussion forum (Ask a question tab on the portal) - is for everyone to ask questions and interact.Anyone who knows the answers can reply to anyone's post and the course instructor/TA will also respond to your queries. Please make maximum use of this feature as this will help you learn much better.
If you have any questions regarding the exam, registration, hall tickets, results, queries related to the technical content in the lectures, any doubts in the assignments, etc can be posted in the forum section

TO GET A CERTIFICATE - PROCESS AND CRITERIA:
The course is free to enroll and learn from. But if you want a certificate, you have to register and write the proctored exam conducted by us in person at any of the designated exam centres.
The exam is optional for a fee of Rs 1000/- (Rupees one thousand only).
Date and Time of Exams: 23 October 2026 Morning session 9am to 12 noon; Afternoon Session 2pm to 5pm.
Registration url: Announcements will be made when the registration form is open for registrations.
The online registration form has to be filled and the certification exam fee needs to be paid. More details will be made available when the exam registration form is published. If there are any changes, it will be mentioned then.
Please check the form for more details on the cities where the exams will be held, the conditions you agree to when you fill the form etc.

CRITERIA TO GET A CERTIFICATE

Average assignment score = 25% of average of best 8 assignments out of the total 12 assignments given in the course.
Exam score = 75% of the proctored certification exam score out of 100

Final score = Average assignment score + Exam score

YOU WILL BE ELIGIBLE FOR A CERTIFICATE ONLY IF AVERAGE ASSIGNMENT SCORE >=10/25 AND EXAM SCORE >= 30/75. If one of the 2 criteria is not met, you will not get the certificate even if the Final score >= 40/100.

Certificate will have your name, photograph and the score in the final exam with the breakup.It will have the logos of NPTEL and IIT Kharagpur. It will be e-verifiable at nptel.ac.in/noc.

Only the e-certificate will be made available. Hard copies will not be dispatched.

Once again, thanks for your interest in our online courses and certification. Happy learning.

- NPTEL team

Content:
Dear Learners,

Due to time zone-related issues, some learners were unable to submit the Week 3 assignment even though the assignment deadline had not yet passed for them.

Considering this, we are extending the deadline for the Week 3 assignment until Friday, August 14, 2026, at 11:59 PM.

Please note that this extension is being provided as a one-time exception. Learners are requested to ensure that their device is configured with the correct time zone and that the system date and time are set to update automatically.

How to set the correct time zone and automatic date/time on your laptop:

  • Windows: Go to Settings → Time & Language → Date & Time.
    • Turn on Set time automatically.
    • Turn on Set time zone automatically.
    • Ensure the correct time zone is selected, if required.
  • Mac: Go to System Settings → General → Date & Time.
    • Enable Set time and date automatically.
    • Enable the option to set the time zone automatically using your current location.

Please make sure your laptop's date, time, and time zone are correctly configured before attempting to submit the assignment.

Mobile submission:
Learners can also submit the assignment using their mobile phones. Please ensure that the mobile device's date, time, and time zone are set automatically to avoid any time-related issues.

Please make use of this extended deadline and submit the Week 3 assignment before Friday, August 14, 2026, 11:59 PM.

Thank you for your cooperation.

Warm regards,
NPTEL Team.

Copyright is an important form of intellectual property right undergoing major transformation due to AI.

Turnip's new course Introduction to Copyrights provides a comprehensive overview of Copyright system to all students, faculty, research scholars and professionals.

Course details

✅   Duration: 8 days (online, self-paced)
✅   Format: Convenient pedagogy (one lesson per day)
✅   Course Fee: No charge! (till 30th Sept.)
✅   Certificate: Upon payment of ₹180/- service fee
✅   Starts immediately after registration and email verification
✅   Course is beginner friendly, suitable for all fields and levels

Lesson Plan

  1. Understanding Copyright
  2. Rights given by Copyright
  3. Infringement vs Fair Use
  4. AI and Copyright
  5. Copyright Societies
  6. Protection of Confidential Information
  7. Copyright Licences and Permissions
  8. Copyright and the Internet
  9. Bonus case study on YouTube

Course Author

This course is created by Dr. Deepika Singh, a leading IPR Expert in India. She is an Advocate, IP Practitioner and a Patent Agent. Subject: AI, Ethics and IP (new course)
Content:
Dear MATHUMITHA,

AI generated content is everywhere! But behind every image, text or app, lies a web of IP and contractual risks.

Turnip's new course AI, Ethics & Intellectual Property shows how to protect what's yours in the AI age. Topics covered:

  • Personality Rights (your name, face, voice)
  • How IP works for AI-generated content
  • IP implications for using data to train AI models
  • AI ethics questions
  • Types of IP protection available for AI ideas
  • How to still be protected in 2035

Course details

✅   Duration: 10 days (online, self-paced)
✅   Format: 10 lessons, one per day via email
✅   Course Fee: No charge!
✅   Certificate: Optional, upon payment of ₹180/- issue fee
✅   Starts immediately after registration and email verification

Course Author

This course is created by Aafreen Collaco, an Advocate and Legal Consultant in IP, privacy and data protection law. She is an LL.M. specialist in IPR & Technology Law and a Ph.D. scholar at Jindal Global Law School, with experience teaching at BITS Law School and Bennett University.

Please share among all students, faculty, innovators and professionals who can benefit.

Thanks and regards,

Neka Sri posted: 🚀 Team Vortex | Smart India Hackathon 2026

We are excited to present our solution for Smart India Hackathon 2026 – Problem Statement 26095: Smart Real-Time Monitoring & Inspection Mobile App.

💡 Our Solution: Edge-AI Powered Infrastructure Inspection Engine

Our idea focuses on making infrastructure inspection smarter, faster, offline, and more reliable using Edge AI.

🔹 Dual Edge-AI Inspection
• Visual AI using YOLOv8-Nano for detecting concrete cracks, rebar exposure and corrosion
• Acoustic AI for identifying transformer arcing and motor fault sounds

🔹 100% Offline Inspection
The system runs directly on smartphones using lightweight TensorFlow Lite models, enabling inspections even in remote areas without internet connectivity.

🔹 Anti-Fraud Security
A 3-layer security approach using GPS verification, dynamic BLE tokens, and QR/serial-tag OCR helps maintain inspection authenticity.

🔹 Hands-Free Inspection
Offline Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech technologies enable voice-based logging and instant defect warnings.

🔹 Secure Local Storage
Inspection data is securely stored using SQLCipher with AES-256 encryption, reducing dependency on cloud infrastructure.

🎯 Our Goal
To enable early detection of infrastructure defects, reduce maintenance costs, improve audit integrity, and contribute to safer bridges, highways, tunnels, substations and power-grid infrastructure.

This presentation was a great opportunity for us to explore how AI + Edge Computing + Mobile Technology + Security can be combined to address real-world infrastructure challenges.

🤝 Proud to be Team Vortex and excited to continue building, learning and innovating together!

Subject: Your free sample of the Medium Newsletter
Content:
https://medium.com

Get the best of Medium delivered to you weekly

 

We hope you’re enjoying your first week on Medium! If you’re looking for a way
to find some interesting writers to follow, we suggest following The Medium
Newsletter <https://medium.com/blog/newsletter?source=mktgemail---mnl>, a weekly
digest of the most interesting and thought-provoking stories on the site.

This sample issue from May 2026 showcases how writing is the key skill of the
A.I. era.

 

Subscribe <https://medium.com/blog/newsletter?source=mktgemail---mnl>

 

https://medium.com/blog/newsletter?source=mktgemail---mnl

AI is making us all writers

Will anyone write (or read) in five years?

If you listen to the breathless coverage of where AI is taking us, the answer
might seem to be "no." Why would we bother communicating with each other when
the robots can do it for us? After all, writing is hard. Why not just spare
ourselves all the effort?

But that's simply not what's happening. Looked at properly, the AI era is
turning everyone into a writer. The major AI tools are all prompt-based, which
is a fancy way of saying "they do what you write." Your ability to capture what
you see in your mind's eye using words is going to be one of the key skills of
the era, and "capturing what you see in your mind's eye"—well friend, that's
just another way of saying "writing."

Writing, as a human practice, isn't going away. At Medium, we love writing
<https://medium.com/p/e30464f2a650?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>. We’ve
never had more writers publishing stories on Medium than we have in 2026. We can
see a very bright future for writing, and we want to do everything we can to
turn that vision into a reality.

So for this week, let's dive into a few recent Medium pieces looking at how
writing and AI are intersecting.

 

The idea that where you sit and when can affect your state of mind might sound
like magic at first. But it’s not, it’s science. Any writer can use the
research-backed power of ritual to make their own writing practice more pleasant
and productive.

—Nir Eyal <https://medium.com/@nireyal?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>, How
to Use the Magic (and Science) of Rituals to Improve Your Writing
<https://medium.com/p/332aca6428b8?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>

 

The essential human ability to judge quality

Educators are on the front line of reckoning with how writing is changing right
now. Tasked with teaching students to think critically and write effectively,
they're now faced with AI-polished (or fully AI-generated) writing that doesn't
reflect a student's actual understanding. Many schools are now starting to focus
on the artifacts of learning that go into student essays—like drafts, notes,
revisions—to assess the process rather than just the output.

While this makes a certain amount of sense, educator Aaron Schultz writes
in Schools Are Solving the Wrong AI Problem
<https://medium.com/p/42c1b80658ba?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>, it's by
no means foolproof. "The trap begins when we assume that documenting the process
is the same as demonstrating learning, when we take evidence that should inform
teaching and turn it into evidence that certifies achievement," Shultz says.

Assessing the process is a category error—students see through it right away,
and turn those notes and drafts into a performance of thinking. The solution?
Asking students follow-up questions that require them to use their judgement.

Judgement, some scholars argue
<https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/02602938.2024.2335321>, has become
the essential human capability in the AI era. Put aside the process and even the
output, and ask students the questions only they can answer for themselves: Is
it good, and if so, why?

 

Some mornings I complain about my life for three pages. Some mornings I untangle
a plot problem or write a shopping list in verse. Sometimes I write about having
nothing to say. More often than not, halfway through, something interesting
emerges.

—Jack Macnamara
<https://medium.com/@johnmcna?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>, As A Writer,
It Took Me 36 Years To Start Doing Morning Pages
<https://medium.com/p/dfab8b500573?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>

 

When AI does (and doesn't) change thinking

You've maybe heard about this study <https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08872>: An MIT
Media Lab researcher last year looked at student brain activity while using
ChatGPT compared to students using Google search or nothing, and found the AI
users "underperformed at neural, linguistic, and behavioral levels." Definitely
concerning! The study was widely covered, and helped spawn the notion AI makes
us dumber <https://medium.com/p/9b58e9d0e153?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>.

But there's nuance to the study that the coverage last year largely missed
<https://medium.com/p/9ce0c5019c08?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>, writes
data scientist Abi Kambanis. First, the negative impact showed up in immediate
cognitive impact (ie, in the moment), but wasn't structural or long term. We
don't, as yet, know what kind of effect AI tools will or won't have on the brain
long-term.

More importantly, the main effect the study looked at, cognitive debt
<https://medium.com/p/5182e4a4fa98?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>, showed up
differently in different AI usage contexts. Yes, when students were using AI to
generate answers and uncritically copying and pasting them, cognitive debt
showed up in the results. But structured AI usage—where AI is used to respond to
the work already written—had much lower impact on cognitive debt.

"What distinguishes these conditions is not the presence or absence of AI, but
the location of human agency within the workflow," Kambanis writes. "When users
retain responsibility for planning, evaluation, and synthesis, AI can function
as a cognitively productive scaffold. When these responsibilities are also
offloaded, engagement declines."

Or, she writes, "In this mode, cognitive effort does not disappear. It
relocates."

 



Source: https://www.threads.com/@helenr/post/DXpTyM5FaeX

 

Be an explorer, not a tourist, when it comes to writing

It's worth keeping in mind in the midst of this discussion of AI and writing
that, sad but true, there was slop writing even before ChatGPT came along. I
know, it's hard to hear, but humans have been making slop as long as writing's
been around.

And the internet, for good and bad, has been home to a lot of it. Not bad
writing per se, but familiar, boring writing, "You open an essay online. The
writing is competent. The sentences are clear. The advice is sensible. And yet,
halfway through, a quiet feeling appears: Wait. Haven’t I read this before?,"
writes David B. Clear in "Why Most Online Writing Feels Like Something You’ve
Already Read
<https://medium.com/p/b59a4257130c?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>."

Clear has a novel metaphor for this: Tourism. The tourist writer shows up at the
same topics like a tourist snapping a picture of the Eiffel Tower. There's no
ill-intent, and everyone's entitled to their tourist pictures (please don't go
look at my Instagram feed), but the sameness leaches out anything meaningful for
the reader to hold on.

The naturalist writer, on the other hand, takes a different approach. They're
not collecting snapshots, they're exploring with the goal of understanding
something deeply. At its core, good writing is about discovery. "The tourist
covers ground and recreates postcards," Clear writers. "The naturalist explores
territory and makes discoveries."

He doesn't say it, but I will: Relying on AI to generate your writing makes you
a tourist no matter what—a tourist to your writing and a tourist to your own
mind. Don't be a tourist.

 

A final thought

We just absolutely loved this recent story about the power of small repairs,
"Minor Mendings
<https://medium.com/p/1cc4d6400c00?source=mktgemail-cd443d43a5e--mnl>," by Karla
L. Miller. If you want, you could probably even apply it to writing, but hey,
I'm not the boss of you!

A key quote:

"If you’re stuck in a space where nothing is urgent but everything needs doing,
and the consequences of delay are yours alone to bear, then Repair of Small
Objects may be just the spell that frees you from your doom spiral."

Neka Sri posted: 📊 Mini Project | AI Impact on Future Jobs 2030 🤖

I’m excited to share my Data Analytics Mini Project – “AI Impact on Future Jobs 2030: AI Workforce Analytics Dashboard."

This project focuses on analyzing how Artificial Intelligence and automation are influencing the future workforce using interactive data visualizations developed in Power BI.🚀

Through this dashboard, I explored:
🔹 AI Replacement Risk across job roles
🔹 Future Job Demand and projected growth
🔹 Salary trends across education levels
🔹 Hiring Trends
🔹 Remote, Hybrid & On-site work patterns
🔹 Automation Levels and AI Tool Usage
🔹 Workforce distribution across countries
🔹 Employee Performance & Job Satisfaction
🔹 Upskilling and workforce development requirements

The project helped me understand how raw workforce data can be transformed into meaningful insights through data visualization and analytics.

🛠️ Tools & Technologies:
Power BI | Data Analytics | Data Visualization | Business Intelligence

🎯 Key Learning:
This mini project strengthened my skills in data analysis, dashboard development, visualization, analytical thinking, and interpreting workforce trends.
It also gave me practical exposure to using data to understand the evolving relationship between AI, automation, jobs, and future career opportunities.
